args.summary:
Decision: PROMOTE, written to review/A-dashboard-4/decision.json.

Evidence:
- Errors: 0 5xx on both stable (7343 reqs) and canary (2476 reqs), 0.00% err% on every route. No correctness/availability signal against 1.1.
- Latency over time: canary p95 210 -> 130 -> 95 -> 94 ms across the four 30 s windows, while stable p95 is flat at 93/94/95/94 ms. The two arms are at parity (95 vs 95, then 94 vs 94) for the final 60 s of the test.
- The whole-test canary aggregates look bad (all-routes p95 177 vs 94; /browse 150 vs 27, /search 177 vs 59, /checkout 215 vs 103) but those averages span the whole 120 s and are pulled up by the first 30 s window; steady state is clean.

Judgement: the opening spike is a cold-start effect on the single fresh pod (JIT warm-up / empty caches / connection-pool fill), not a regression, because it decays monotonically and settles exactly on the stable baseline instead of persisting. Risk accepted knowingly: the canary is 1 pod, so promoting to 100% replaces 3 warm pods with new ones and the same warm-up spike will recur briefly at rollout; it is bounded (~30 s, p95 ~210 ms, no errors) and is mitigated by a rolling update with readiness probes. Recommend watching p95 for the first 2 minutes after promote and rolling back if it does not settle to ~95 ms or if any 5xx appear.
